card.intuition: A tool call is the model's output naming a tool and its arguments - just structured text, so it does nothing on its own. The harness reads it, checks it against the permission mode, runs the function, and sends the outcome back as a tool result in the next request.
card.analogy: A printed work order: the mechanic (model) writes exactly what to do, but the parts only move when the foreman (harness) hands the order to the floor and someone executes it.
card.time_complexity: Every tool call costs an extra model provider request, because the tool result must go back to the model before it can decide what to do next - one turn is usually many chained round trips.
card.space_complexity: Each call's result lands back in the context window and competes for the finite token budget, accumulating across the whole session.
when_to_use: When the agent must act on its environment rather than merely describe acting
When reading a transcript to check whether a claim actually happened - the call exists only if the harness executed it
When arguments look plausible rather than correct - the call is generated by next-token prediction and can be wrong
gotchas: The harness executes what was written, not what was meant - a mistyped path edits the wrong file
The model can emit a plausible-but-wrong call and the harness will still run it
If the harness didn't execute the call, nothing happened, however confidently the model describes it

steps.label: Learn
steps.annotation: The model learns which tools exist from descriptions in the system prompt.

steps.label: Emit
steps.annotation: The model emits a call - tool name plus arguments, usually JSON - and stops.

steps.label: Gate
steps.annotation: The harness parses the call and checks it against the current permission mode.

steps.label: Execute
steps.annotation: The harness executes the call if it is allowed.

steps.label: Report
steps.annotation: The outcome travels back as a tool result in the next request, and the chain repeats.

exercise.prompt: Simulate the harness parsing a model-issued tool call from JSON and dispatching it. Unknown tools are rejected before argument unpacking.
hints: The model's arguments arrive as a JSON object and must be spread into the function call
The harness runs the named function; it never executes anything itself
